title: Correct junta decision with no free relevant coordinates
statement: Let $f$ be a sign-valued function on the Boolean cube, let $J$ and $P$ be sets of coordinates, and fix values on the coordinates in $P$. Suppose that $f$ depends only on coordinates in $J$, that $|J\setminus P|\le 0$, and that a decision for the restriction of $f$ to the fixed assignment is correct. Then the decision is a constant decision: there is a sign value that it returns for every assignment to the remaining coordinates.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional cube.
$J$ and $P$ are finite sets of coordinates.
$z$ assigns a sign to each coordinate in $P$.
The function depends only on coordinates in $J$.
The set difference $J\setminus P$ has cardinality at most zero.
The decision is correct for the restriction determined by $z$.
